messages:
ashok: heads up — saw a repeating p99 latency spike on canary when act-quant is enabled with slew_rate=0.8 and prefetch=2 :thinking:

maria: can you paste the config and a quick timeline?

ashok: config snip:
```
model: gpt-large-v2
quant: awq
act_quant: true
group_size: 32
slew_rate: 0.8
prefetch: 2
batch_timeout_ms: 12
```
observed pattern: every ~45s p99 goes +120ms for ~6s then back down, throughput drops ~18% during the bump.

liz: interesting. does the KV cache miss correlate? any big prefix churn? :eyes:

ashok: checked traces — KV hit rate dips from 97% -> 64% during spikes, and GPU utilization briefly drops (cuda streams stall). logs show many small prefetch requests queued.

sam: hypothesis: prefetch=2 is racing with actq kernel warmup/queueing and slew_rate amplification causes batching to oscillate. prefetch floods prefix cache, causing heavier mem copies and eviction thrash.

ben: have we tried lowering group_size? smaller group -> less per-batch memory pressure.

ashok: ran quick local canary tests: group_size=16 reduced amplitude of spikes by ~60%, p99 still 25ms above baseline though. disabling prefetch removed most spikes but increased avg latency by ~10ms.

maria: can you share the minimal repro command you used?

ashok: repro curl (canary):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.internal.redwood/api/generate \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
 -d '{"model":"gpt-large-v2","prompt":"<test-burst>","max_tokens":128,"stream":false}'
```
run in a tight loop with 40 concurrent clients for 5m. script attached in the canary job.

liz: ok, two-pronged experiment plan: 1) reduce group_size to 12 and batch_timeout_ms to 8, keep prefetch=2; 2) keep group_size but set prefetch=0 and bump batch_timeout to 20 to let batching be more stable. run each for 10m and compare KV hit, p99, and GPU stalls.

sam: also add telemetry for actq kernel init latency and stream queue length (we've lacked that metric). can we flip tracing on for 1% of requests?

ashok: enabled tracing for 1% and scheduled both canaries. starting run A now. will post results.

ci-bot: canary-run:3849234567-A started by ashok on canary-cluster-3 at 2026-03-20T15:22:10Z

ashok: run A finished quick summary: p99 amplitude dropped 62%, KV hit steadier (~92%), GPU stall events reduced but actq kernel cold starts still visible at first batch window.

maria: run B (prefetch=0) results?

ashok: run B summary: no sawtooth, p99 lower than baseline during steady state, but tail under bursty arrival increases slightly (avg +8ms). KV hit stable ~95%. overall prefer run A for our traffic shape.

ben: sounds like prefetch helps steady bursts but interacts poorly with actq slew. next steps: tweak slew_rate down to 0.5 in run A config and re-evaluate; instrument actq kernel warmup count.

liz: agree. also create a fallback policy for dedicated: if p99 > baseline+100ms for 2 consecutive windows, route to non-actq variant automatically.

ashok: noted. I'll run slew_rate=0.5/ group_size=12/ batch_timeout=8 next and attach traces. thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — add a short note to the model onboarding doc about this interaction so future canaries include the prefetch/slew checklist.

ashok: will do and will open a tiny RFC for a telemetry field to expose kernel warmups to console.

ci-bot: canary-run:3849234567-B completed by ashok at 2026-03-20T15:30:20Z

ashok: run B final: slew_rate=0.5 results look good — p99 within +12ms of baseline, KV hit 94%, no oscillation in 15m run. rolling this config to a 5% soft rollout now.

liz: nice work. keep eyes on long-tail regressions over the next 24h.

sam: filed follow-ups: TICKET-ML-482 (telemetry), TICKET-ML-483 (onboarding checklist).

ashok: closing thread, will post RFC link when created.
